title: Louis Cottrell Jr., Arthur Derbigny and Don Albert breaking up the band
summary: Ridgley says Cottrell played with him briefly, and that Don Albert took Cottrell and Derbigny and broke up his band.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: This is Real Thor, Bebe Ridgely, April 11th, 1961. I wondered about Louis Cottrell Jr., the clarinet player and saxophone player.

Let me see what time could that have been. He didn't stay too long. He was playing with me and another fellow came in. Let me see the name of my 20th player. He was playing with saxophone and Derby. He's dead. Arthur Derby is a violin player he was with me.
Derby is alive I believe. Is he?
Somebody told me he was dead. I saw him a couple of years ago.
He may be dead now. I don't know.
And so Louis hadn't been with me alone. This fellow came in and took Louis and Derby and broke up my band and went on off. I forgot that guy in there. He had a big band.
The trumpet player that went out to Texas?
Yeah. What's his name? Don Albert. Yeah. I want to show you a picture in a book over here. Has he still got his band?
No, no. He has a nightclub out there here.
Oh, I see. He was a good clarinet player.
Yeah, I believe he is. What they say about him. And he made a few records himself. Yeah.
He's a good band in the new one.
